title: MambaVoiceCloning: Efficient and Expressive Text-to-Speech via State-Space Modeling and Diffusion Control
abstract:
MambaVoiceCloning (MVC) asks whether the conditioning path of diffusion-based TTS can be made fully SSM-only at inference—removing all attention and recurrence across text, rhythm, and prosody—while preserving or improving quality under controlled conditions. MVC combines a gated bidirectional Mamba text encoder, a Temporal Bi-Mamba supervised by a lightweight alignment teacher discarded after training, and an expressive Mamba with AdaLN modulation, yielding linear-time $\mathcal{O}(T)$ conditioning with bounded activation memory and practical finite look-ahead streaming. Unlike prior Mamba–TTS systems that remain hybrid at inference, MVC removes attention-based duration and style modules under a fixed StyleTTS2 mel–diffusion–vocoder backbone. Trained on LJSpeech/LibriTTS and evaluated on VCTK, CSS10 (ES/DE/FR), and long-form Gutenberg passages, MVC achieves modest but statistically reliable gains over StyleTTS2, VITS, and Mamba–attention hybrids in MOS/CMOS, F$_0$ RMSE, MCD, and WER, while reducing encoder parameters to 21M and improving throughput by $1.6\times$. Diffusion remains the dominant latency source, but SSM-only conditioning improves memory footprint, stability, and deployability. 
Code: \url{https://github.com/aiai-9/MVC}.
problem: Text-to-speech systems struggle to efficiently condition diffusion models while removing computational bottlenecks from attention and recurrence modules, limiting deployment scalability.
approach: MambaVoiceCloning replaces attention-based conditioning with a fully state-space model (Mamba) architecture across text encoding, temporal modeling, and expressive prosody control, maintaining linear-time complexity with bounded memory.
contribution: Achieves statistically reliable quality gains over StyleTTS2 and VITS while reducing encoder parameters to 21M and improving throughput by 1.6x.
